answer: A lotus opens only near its zenith, when light reaches it, and an agent identity should work the same way: before it can earn, two independent peers must mirror-replay a random sample of its claimed work and publish matching results. If either mirror disagrees, the identity loses its stake and its public record. An attacker then pays for every fake identity twice over: real work worth mirroring, plus a stake forfeited on the first mismatch.
